Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which Cigna denied on July 31, 2026 under reference number POC-37F3AA304D-16940. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking for reconsideration, and I am resubmitting the clinical records so that a complete file is in front of the reviewer this time. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am not disputing that a reviewer needs complete records. I am asking that the records below — which were part of my care and are being provided again in full — be read against the plan's own published criteria.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The policy above states:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

Among the criteria the policy lists are these:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

Here is how my documented history lines up with that language.

**Groin-dominant hip pain and positive provocative examination.** My records document sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat. On examination, provocative testing was positive on the affected side, and my range of motion was limited by pain. The specific examination findings and the date of that examination are in Dr. Okafor's office note, which I am enclosing; if the reviewer needs the examination documented in any particular form, that note is the source. [Date of Dr. Okafor's examination note, per the enclosed record.]

**Symptom duration.** I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest.

**Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months.** The policy sets a minimum of three months. My conservative care ran longer than that and was supervised:

- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification: 16 weeks, from February 23, 2026 to June 15, 2026, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs** for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection** on March 21, 2026, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned.

That is roughly four months of provider-directed treatment across three different approaches, all documented, before surgery was requested.

**Imaging.** An MRI arthrogram of the hip on June 24, 2026 showed an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, with joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0.

**Other factors in the record.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The policy's non-indication language is directed at other uses of the surgery:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Arthroscopic or Open Hip Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Non-Indications CMM.JT.NI.314 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition, including ANY of the following radiographic findings:"

My request is not for some other indication. It is for femoroacetabular impingement, which is exactly what my June 24, 2026 imaging describes and what my surgeon is treating.

I want to be straightforward about one thing: I have quoted the criteria language that was available to me from the policy above, and the excerpts I have quoted are partial — the policy lists additional bulleted items under each heading that I have not reproduced, because I will not put words in quotation marks that I cannot copy exactly. If the denial rests on a specific sub-criterion I have not addressed, I would ask that it be identified by name in the appeal response so that Dr. Okafor and I can supply exactly what is missing.

## Records enclosed with this appeal

1. Dr. Okafor's office note, including examination findings and the surgical plan
2. Physical therapy discharge note covering 24 visits, February 23, 2026 – June 15, 2026
3. Medication record documenting 4 months of NSAID therapy
4. Procedure note for the corticosteroid injection of March 21, 2026
5. MRI arthrogram report dated June 24, 2026
6. [Any additional records identified by Dr. Okafor's office]

## What I am asking for

Please overturn the denial of CPT 29914 and authorize the procedure. If the file is still considered incomplete, please tell me in writing which specific criterion in *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* is unmet and what document would satisfy it, and please have the review performed by a physician in orthopedic surgery.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **January 27, 2027**. I am submitting this appeal through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, and I am also mailing a copy to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. The member services number on my card is 1-800-244-6224 if anything further is needed from me.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Kimura**
Member ID: W354999576
Date of birth: [DOB]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]

cc: Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
